data.content_ref: inline:Replace the skeptical fixed-point over labels with a proof-theoretic grounded consequence relation: a node is accepted iff there exists a finite derivation tree using two rules — an attacker rule that discharges an attack when the attacker is refuted, and a warrant rule that introduces a committed root — and the extension is the set of formulas derivable in this monotone sequent calculus. The fixed point is recovered as the least Herbrand model of the derivation rules, preserving determinism and polynomial cost because derivability in a Horn fragment is P-complete; reinstatement is a derived theorem, not an extra postulate. This makes provenance internal to the derivation rather than an attached trace. Criticism: it may make the semantics less modular and harder to extend with quantitative information.
